Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE6243 : Soft Computing Techniques { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Optimization Techniques (12 Hours)
- Preliminary Mathematics: Matrix Calculus, Taylor Series Expansion, Convex Set and Convex Function
- Convex Optimization:
- Unconstrained Optimization by Steepest Descent Method
- Newton’s Method and LMDN Method
- Conjugate Gradient Method
- Constrained Optimization
- Nonconvex Optimization:
- Genetic Algorithm (GA)
- Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)
-
Module 2: Introduction to Machine Learning (22 Hours)
- Regression:
- Linear and Polynomial Regression
- Classification by Logistic Regression
- Artificial Neural Network:
- Supervised Learning:
- Input-Output Mapping and Classification by Adaptive Linear Model
- Multi-Layer Perceptron: Back-Propagation Learning
- Radial Basis Function Neural Network
- Unsupervised Learning:
- Clustering by Self-Organizing Maps
- Support Vector Machine
-
Module 3: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) (4 Hours)

To learn different types of optimization techniques.
2 .

To learn structure, training methods and applications of artificial neural networks.
3 .

To design fuzzy controllers/fuzzy rule based systems

At the end of the course, students will be able to
Analyze different types of optimization problems and apply appropriate optimization techniques to solve them.

2 .

Apply meta-heuristic methods to effectively solve nonconvex optimization problems
3 .

Implement single and multi-layer perceptrons for input-output mapping and classification problems.
4 .

Apply clustering techniques to categorize datasets based on patterns and relationships.

Utilize Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction in large-scale data processing.

Develop and evaluate machine learning models for real-world industrial applications.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PA3611 : Acoustics and Illumination { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I- Basic theory of sound:
Frequency, wavelength, velocity, sound spectrum, the sensitivity of hearing inverse-square law, decibel, noise exposure limits sound level meters, A-Weighted sound level decibel scales for sound intensity, pressure and power.
Assignment: Numerical exercises on intensity to dB conversion and inverse-square law
Module II- Sound absorption:
Sound absorbing treatment sound absorption coefficient, reverberation room application of sound-absorbing materials reverberation time, optimum reverberation time.
Assignment(s): Numerical exercises on sound absorption and reverberation time calculations for a built space.
Module III- Sound reflections:
Sight line basics sight line layout, reflection diffusion, diffraction, ray diagram graphics echoes, echo control principles, flutter echo.
Assignment: Exercises on ray-diagram analysis of a built space and identifying the causes of echo.
Module IV- Sound isolation:
Mass law, effect of stiffness sound leaks, noise reduction between rooms, STC contour masking for sound isolation, noise criteria curves, room criteria curves impact isolation outdoor barrier for noise control, thin-wall barrier, balconies and overhangs, earth berms attenuation from vegetation temperature and wind effect, land use planning for noise control, orientation of buildings.
Assignment: Exercise on proposing various strategies for isolating outside sound for a building.
Module V- Basic concept in lighting:
Qualities of light sources lamps and luminaires quality of light, quantity of light for an enclosed space lighting design approach and lighting design in spaces like residential, workplace, classroom, healthcare, retail, hospitality, common spaces outdoor lighting design.
Assignment: Exercise on describing the properties of lamps and luminaire design.
Module VI- Daylighting:
Basic principles of daylighting daylighting systems case-study on daylighting and illumination, including use of software to assess daylighting conditions

Course Objective

1 .

To acquire and apply knowledge of basic building sciences related to acoustics while proposing acoustical solutions
2 .

To develop an understanding of various types of luminaires and lamps and apply the same in proposing illumination design.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Ability to develop an understanding of the sound absorption, reflection, and transmission of sound in enclosed space.
2. Ability to draw the acoustical ray-diagram and analyse an architectural space for any acoustical defects and propose solutions.
3. Ability to analyse the quantitative and qualitative demand of lighting in a space, and to propose an illumination design.
4. Ability to understand the principles of daylighting and strategies to integrate daylighting inside the building.

Egan, M. D., Architectural Acoustics, New Castle: J. Ross Publishing

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CS6220 : Computer Vision { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

UNIT I
Introduction : Image Processing, Computer Vision and Computer Graphics , What is Computer Vision - Low-level, Mid-level, High-level , Overview of Diverse Computer Vision Applications: Document Image, Analysis, Bio-metrics, Object Recognition, Tracking, Medical Image Analysis, Content-Based Image Retrieval, Video Data Processing, Multimedia, Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality.
UNIT II
Image Formation Models : Monocular imaging system , Orthographic & Perspective Projection, Camera model and Camera calibration, Binocular imaging systems, Multiple views geometry, Structure determination, shape from shading , Photometric Stereo, Depth from Defocus , Construction of 3D model from images.
UNIT III
Image Processing, Feature Extraction, and Motion Estimation : Image pre-processing, Image representations (continuous and discrete) , Edge detection, Regularization theory , Optical computation ,Stereo Vision , Motion estimation , Structure from motion.
UNIT IV
Shape Representation and Segmentation: Contour based representation, Region based representation, De-formable curves and surfaces , Snakes and active contours, Level set representations , Fourier, and wavelet descriptors , Medial representations , Multi-resolution analysis, Object recognition.
UNIT V
Image Understanding and Computer Vision Applications: Pattern recognition methods, Face detection, Face recognition, 3D shape models of faces Application: Surveillance – foreground-background separation –human gait analysis Application: In-vehicle vision system: locating roadway – road markings – identifying road signs – locating pedestrians.

Course Objective

1 .

Describe the foundation of image formation and image analysis. Understand the basics of 2D and 3D Computer Vision.
2 .

Become familiar with the major technical approaches involved in computer vision. Describe various methods used for registration, alignment, and matching in images.
3 .

Perform shape analysis and extract features form Images and do analysis of Images
4 .

Get an exposure to advanced concepts, including state of the art deep learning architectures, in all aspects of computer vision.

Course Outcome

1 .

Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1.Know the theoretical and practical aspects of computing with images and the foundation of image formation, measurement, and analysis
2. Implement common methods for robust image matching and alignment
3. Understand the geometric relationships between 2D images and the 3D world
4. Gain exposure to object and scene recognition and categorization from images
5. Develop the practical skills necessary to build computer vision applications.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MN6072 : Mine System Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Lab 1: Introduction to mathematical formulation of optimization problem for a defined mining systems and Software for solving the problems.
Lab 2: Formulation of linear programming problem (LPP) for a defined mining system and solve using suitable software or computer programming. Generation and interpretation of sensitivity analysis of the defined problem.
Lab 3: Formulation of transportation problem for a defined mining system as LPP and Solve using suitable software or computer programming.
Lab 4: Formulation of integer programming problem for a defined mining system and solve using suitable software or computer programming.
Lab 5: Formulation of assignment problem as an Integer programming problem and solve using suitable software.
Lab 6: Formulation of dynamic programming problem for a defined mining system (pit optimization/maximized NPV) and solve using suitable computer programming.
Lab 7: Determination of best Fitting Probability Distribution Curve for a typical field data of a mining systems.
Lab 8: Simulation for optimizing the queuing system in mines.
Lab 9: Reliability analysis of a mining system for estimating the schedule maintenance time using suitable software or computer programming.
Lab 10: Mathematical formulation of non-linear programming problem for a defined mining system and solving using suitable software or computer programming.
Lab 11: Mathematical formulation of the inventory for a defined mining system and solving using suitable software or computer programming.
Lab 12: Introduction to evolutionary algorithms for solving the optimization problems of a defined mining system.

Course Objective

1 .

The primary objective is to develop skills for mathematical formulation of the optimizations problems for different mining systems
2 .

The other objective of the course is to develop skills for writing computer programming or handling optimization software for solving the optimization problems.

Course Outcome

1 .

By the end of this course, students will be able to:
CO1: Develop necessary software skills for defining a mining systems and mathematical formulation of the problems.
CO2: Develop necessary software skills and methods to optimize the mining systems.

Essential Reading

1 .

LINDO Systems, Inc., LINDO USER's Manual, LINDO Systems, Inc , USA

2 .

A. K. Gorai, Instruction Manual, NIT Rourkela

Subject {L-T-P / C} : SM6332 : Strategic Human Resource Management { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Overview of Business Environment & Strategic Management: Levels of Strategy, Strategic Planning, Strategic Management & HR Linkages. Strategic HRM: Concept, Process, Steps Involved Linking Business Strategy and HR strategy, Formulating and Implementing HR strategy. Aspects of Strategic Human Resource Management (SHRM): Organization Development, Change Management, Culture, Recruitment & Selection, Performance Management and Employee Development, Reward Management, Employee Relation. Strategic Employee Retention, Restructuring and Strategic HR: Employee Retention Challenges, Methods of Retention, Strategic Restructuring, Talent Management and Competency Mapping. Strategies for Improving Organizational Effectiveness: Strategies for Organizational Transformations - Cross Border Mergers & Acquisitions, Strategies for Culture Management, Quality in Strategies, Strategies for Learning Organizations, Employee Engagement and Strategies.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the concept of strategic human resource management and explore how the strategic approach to human resources is different from the traditional approach
2 .

To understand how the development, implementation and evaluation of change occurs in a dynamic business environment

Course Outcome

1 .

How an organization deals with its people – realization of the strategic importance of this aspect in the success of an organization has led to the evolution of Strategic Human Resource Management. The course will help to gain an insight on the strategic approach towards HRM and to understand, how various HR strategies are formulated and implemented.
